questions.prompt: Why does a pointer chase measure latency rather than bandwidth?
options: Each load's address depends on the previous load's result, so nothing can overlap
questions.explanation: Dependent loads serialise: time per access is latency.

questions.prompt: In a latency-vs-size curve, what marks a cache's capacity?
options: The size at which the latency steps up
questions.explanation: Steps are capacities; plateaus are latencies.

questions.prompt: What's the general recipe for a microbenchmark?
options: Run a real application and average
Make run time depend on one hidden property, vary one parameter, and find where the time changes
questions.explanation: Isolate one effect, sweep one variable.

questions.prompt: According to the paper, why can reordering register numbers make Volta code faster?
options: Operands in the same register bank conflict and cost extra cycles
questions.explanation: Register bank conflicts: a compiler (or hand-written assembly) can avoid them.

questions.prompt: To measure a cache's line (or sector) size, what do you sweep?
questions.explanation: Cost per access grows with stride until each access needs its own line.
